name: lemma-reuse
label: Сначала точное переиспользование леммы
instructions: Before constructing a new proof, look for an accepted lemma that closes the exact goal or reduces it to explicit obligations. Use native Lean matching when available. Similar statements are not interchangeable. A reuse proposal requires the usual Lean verification and independent review.

procedure: Search accepted current lemmas by domain, parameters and conclusion before writing a new proof.
Inspect the exact type, module, revision and verification status of each plausible lemma.
Use native Lean matching to establish the substitution when available; otherwise mark applicability as unverified.
Turn every unmatched logical premise into a separate obligation and never hide or assume it.
If the match is exact, construct the smallest import-and-apply candidate using the pinned module and declaration.
If no exact match exists, report that result and choose another method without forcing a similar lemma.
Submit the resulting application to the normal Lean verification and independent review path.
preconditions: The exact consumer goal is pinned and its dependencies are explicit.
Only accepted current library revisions are eligible for automatic reuse.
inputs: Accepted lemma signatures, native inspection and match reports.
Pinned module imports and unresolved application obligations.
contract.output: Either a minimal role-required proof candidate that applies an exact accepted lemma, or an explicit no-exact-match report listing rejected candidates and unresolved premises. No reuse claim is itself mathematical verification.
stop_criteria: Stop after producing one exact application candidate for verification or establishing that the bounded search found no exact match.
Stop rather than reuse a lemma with unresolved types, stale revisions or hidden premises.
examples: Success: a native match proves the consumer type by an accepted theorem and leaves one explicit arithmetic premise as a separate goal.
Failure: a lemma with a visually similar conclusion but a different finite index type is rejected instead of being applied by textual similarity.
